arrow.context: A solid mouse pointer tilted to the upper left, the default cursor on desktop screens. Used in tutorials, design tools for the select tool, and buttons that switch back to pointer mode.

arrow-autofit-height.context: A vertical double-headed arrow between a top bar and a bottom bar. Used for fit to height, auto height and stretch vertically options in spreadsheets, table editors and layout tools.

arrow-autofit-width.context: A horizontal double-headed arrow between a left bar and a right bar. Found in spreadsheets and table editors as the autofit column width command, and in layout tools as fit to width or fill container.

arrow-bar-down.context: An arrow pointing down into a horizontal bar. Means move to bottom, jump to the end of a list, align bottom or send a layer to the back in some editors.

arrow-bar-left.context: An arrow pointing left into a vertical bar. Used for go to start, first page, align left, collapse a sidebar to the left edge and jump to the beginning of a line.

arrow-bar-right.context: An arrow pointing right into a vertical bar. Used for go to end, last page, align right, expand a panel to the right edge and jump to the end of a line.

arrow-bar-up.context: An arrow pointing up into a horizontal bar. Common as back to top and scroll to top buttons, align top in layout tools and upload or bring to front actions.

arrow-big-down.context: A thick block arrow pointing down, drawn as an outlined shape with a wide head. Good for download prompts, signage, voting down and large directional cues in kiosks and slides.

arrow-big-left.context: A thick outlined block arrow pointing left. Used as a large back or previous button, on signage and for leftward directions in presentations and kiosk screens.

arrow-big-right.context: A thick outlined block arrow pointing right. Common as a large next or continue button, on wayfinding signs and in slides to show a step or flow.

arrow-big-up.context: A thick outlined block arrow pointing up. Used for upvotes, upload prompts, shift key hints and large upward cues on signs and slides.

arrow-circle-down.context: A down arrow inside a circle. Seen on download buttons, scroll down hints on landing pages and expandable sections.

arrow-circle-left.context: A left arrow inside a circle. Works as a round back or previous button in carousels, galleries, wizards and step-by-step forms.

arrow-circle-up.context: An up arrow inside a circle. Used for back to top buttons, upload actions and upward direction markers.

arrow-curve-left.context: An arrow that arches from the right over the top and ends pointing down on the left. Used for counter-clockwise turns, undo-style jumps, flow diagrams and routing directions.

arrow-curve-right.context: An arrow that arches from the left over the top and ends pointing down on the right. Used for clockwise turns, skip or jump steps in flow diagrams and routing directions.

arrow-down.context: A plain straight arrow pointing down. Used for scroll down hints, download links, sort order, values going down and any downward direction.

arrow-down-left.context: A straight arrow pointing diagonally toward the lower left corner. Used for incoming items such as received payments, inbound calls and messages, and for southwest directions.

arrow-down-right.context: A straight arrow pointing diagonally toward the lower right corner. Used for southeast directions, drop in value markers and resize corner hints.

arrow-left.context: A plain straight arrow pointing left. The standard back button in app headers and browsers, the previous control in carousels and pagers, and a west direction marker.

arrow-loop.context: A line that runs right, rises into a small loop and continues right to an arrowhead. Used for indirect paths, retries, workflow loops and detours in diagrams and route guides.

arrow-narrow-down.context: A long, thin arrow with a small head pointing down. Fits sort indicators in table headers, scroll hints and compact down arrows beside text.

arrow-narrow-left.context: A long, thin arrow with a small head pointing left. Used for text links like back to blog, previous article and understated back buttons.

arrow-narrow-right.context: A long, thin arrow with a small head pointing right. Often placed after link text such as read more, learn more or continue, and in minimal next buttons.

arrow-narrow-up.context: A long, thin arrow with a small head pointing up. Used for sort ascending indicators, back to top links and small upward change markers.

arrow-return.context: An arrow that curls from the top right around and back along the bottom to point left. Used for return, go back, revert changes and the enter or return key.

arrow-right.context: A plain straight arrow pointing right. The standard next, continue or submit arrow in buttons, links, carousels, wizards and forms, and an east direction marker.

arrow-right-circle.context: A right arrow inside a circle. Used as a round next or go button in carousels, onboarding flows, search boxes and call to action links.

arrow-square-down.context: A down arrow inside a rounded square. Used as a boxed download button, a move down control in list editors and a select or dropdown hint.

arrow-square-left.context: A left arrow inside a rounded square. Used for boxed back or previous buttons and to show the left arrow key in keyboard shortcut guides.

arrow-square-right.context: A right arrow inside a rounded square. Used for boxed next or go buttons and for the right arrow key in keyboard shortcut guides and game controls.

arrow-square-up.context: An up arrow inside a rounded square. Used for boxed upload buttons, move up controls in list editors and the up arrow key in shortcut guides.

arrow-up.context: A plain straight arrow pointing up. Used for upload, back to top, sort ascending, rising values, upvotes and any upward direction.

arrow-up-left.context: A straight arrow pointing diagonally toward the upper left corner. Used for northwest directions, going back up a level and pulling an item back from a corner.

arrow-up-right.context: A straight arrow pointing diagonally toward the upper right corner. Common as the external link or open in new tab mark, for outgoing payments and calls, and for growth or upward change.

arrow-zigzag.context: A line that goes down, cuts back up diagonally, drops again and ends in an arrow pointing up. Used for winding or indirect paths, volatile progress and non-linear processes.

arrows-cross.context: Two diagonal arrows crossing in an X, both pointing to the right side. Used for crossing paths, swap or transfer between two lanes, intersections and random order.

arrows-diagonal.context: Two parallel diagonal arrows pointing opposite ways, one to the upper right and one to the lower left. Used for two-way traffic, exchange, send and receive, and diagonal resize.

arrows-left-right.context: A single horizontal line with an arrowhead at each end. Used for horizontal resize, width, left and right movement, back and forth motion and two-way links.

arrows-maximize.context: Four arrows pointing out toward the four corners. Used to maximize, enlarge, go full screen, expand an image or scale a shape up.

arrows-minimize.context: Four arrows pointing in from the four corners toward the centre. Used to minimize, shrink, exit full screen, compress a view or scale down.

arrows-shuffle.context: Two straight arrows with angled bends that cross over each other, both pointing right. Used for shuffle play, random order, swapping lanes and mixing items.

arrows-up-down.context: A single vertical line with an arrowhead at each end. Used for vertical resize, height, up and down movement, sort order toggles and two-way data.

caret-down.context: A small solid triangle pointing down. Marks dropdown menus and select boxes, descending sort order in table headers and open tree nodes.

caret-left.context: A small solid triangle pointing left. Used as a compact back or previous control, a collapsed panel toggle and a pointer on speech bubbles or tooltips.

caret-right.context: A small solid triangle pointing right. Used for collapsed tree nodes and disclosure rows, compact next controls and submenu indicators.

caret-up.context: A small solid triangle pointing up. Marks ascending sort in table headers, open dropdowns, collapse toggles and upvote or increase controls.

chevron-down.context: A simple V-shaped chevron pointing down. The usual mark for dropdown menus, accordions, expand sections, select fields and scroll down hints.

chevron-left.context: A simple chevron pointing left. The common back button in mobile app headers, the previous control in carousels, calendars and pagination, and a collapse sidebar toggle.

chevron-left-right.context: A left chevron and a right chevron side by side, pointing away from each other. Used for code and embed buttons, horizontal scrolling, carousels and expand width controls.

chevron-right.context: A simple chevron pointing right. Marks list rows that open a detail view, collapsed tree items, next buttons in carousels and calendars, and breadcrumb separators.

chevron-up.context: A simple chevron pointing up. Used to collapse accordions and panels, close dropdowns, show less and scroll back to top.

chevron-up-down.context: An up chevron stacked over a down chevron. Marks select menus and pickers, sortable table columns and elements that can be expanded or collapsed.

chevrons-down.context: Two stacked chevrons pointing down. Used for expand all, scroll to bottom, show everything, and strong downward cues such as a big drop.

chevrons-left.context: Two chevrons side by side pointing left. Used for first page in pagination, rewind or skip back, and collapse sidebar toggles.

chevrons-right.context: Two chevrons side by side pointing right. Used for last page in pagination, skip forward, fast forward and expand sidebar toggles.

chevrons-up.context: Two stacked chevrons pointing up. Used for collapse all, scroll to top, priority or rank increases and strong upward cues.

collapse.context: Two diagonal arrows, one from the top right and one from the bottom left, pointing in toward the centre. Used to collapse a panel, shrink a window, exit full screen or scale down.

compass-arrow.context: A circle with a diamond-shaped compass needle tilted toward the top right. Used for explore and discover sections, bearings, orientation and navigation apps.

corner-down-left.context: An arrow that runs down, then turns and points left. Used for the enter or return key, new line, reply and send actions in chat inputs.

corner-down-right.context: An arrow that runs down, then turns and points right. Used for nested replies and sub-items, indent, child rows in tables and follow-on steps.

corner-left-up.context: An arrow that runs left, then turns and points up. Used for turn directions, go up a level to the parent folder and upward flow in diagrams.

corner-right-up.context: An arrow that runs right, then turns and points up. Used for turn directions, move up a level and upward steps in flow diagrams.

corner-up-left.context: An arrow that rises, then turns and points left. Used for reply, back, turn left in directions and moving an item up and back in flow diagrams.

corner-up-right.context: An arrow that rises, then turns and points right. Used for forward or share actions, turn right in directions and next steps in flow diagrams.

crosshair.context: A circle crossed by four short ticks, one at each side. Used for precise positioning, locate me buttons, aiming, targeting and color picker or measuring tools.

cursor-text.context: The I-beam text cursor, a vertical line with short serifs at top and bottom. Used for text tools, editable fields, text selection and type or insert text actions.

direction.context: A signpost with a single board pointing right on a short post. Used for directions, wayfinding, finding the way, road signs and trail or route guides.

drag-horizontal.context: A pair of vertical bars with small arrows pointing left and right. Marks a split pane or column divider that can be dragged sideways, and horizontal resize handles.

drag-vertical.context: A pair of horizontal bars with small arrows pointing up and down. Marks a split pane or row divider that can be dragged up and down, and vertical resize handles.

enter.context: An arrow moving right into an open ring. Used for enter, go inside, join a room or call, import and access actions.

exit.context: An arrow leaving an open ring and pointing right. Used for exit, leave a room or call, quit an app, export and go out actions.

expand.context: Two diagonal arrows, one to the top right and one to the bottom left, pointing out from the centre. Used to expand a panel, open a larger view, enlarge media or go full screen.

focus.context: Four corner brackets framing a small centre dot. Used for autofocus and camera focus points, scan areas, focus mode and centring a view.

fork.context: A straight arrow pointing up with a second arrow branching off to the upper right. Used for forks in the road, branching paths, forking a project and alternative routes.

forward-mail.context: An arrow with a curved tail pointing right. The forward action in email and chat apps, used to pass a message on to someone else or share it.

fullscreen.context: Four corner brackets with their corners facing outward. The enter full screen button in video players, slideshows, maps and games.

fullscreen-exit.context: Four corner brackets with their corners turned inward. The exit full screen button in video players, slideshows and games.

grab.context: A closed hand gripping, seen from the back. The grabbing cursor for dragging a canvas or map, moving items, and the hand or pan tool in design apps.

login.context: An arrow pointing right into a door-like bracket. The sign in or log in action on account pages, headers and access screens.

logout.context: An arrow pointing right out of a door-like bracket. The sign out or log out action in account menus and settings.

maximize.context: A window with a diagonal arrow pointing toward its top right corner. Used to maximize a window, open a panel in a larger view or pop out a widget.

merge.context: Two lines from the lower corners that join into one arrow pointing up. Used for merging branches in version control, combining lanes, joining data and merge cells.

minimize.context: A window with a diagonal arrow pointing to its bottom left corner. Used to minimize a window, shrink a panel back into place or dock a widget.

move.context: A cross of four arrows pointing up, down, left and right. The move tool in design and image apps, used for dragging, panning and repositioning items.

move-diagonal.context: A double-headed arrow running diagonally from the lower left to the upper right. Used for diagonal resize handles, scaling from a corner and stretching an element.

navigation.context: A solid arrowhead pointing up and to the right, like a map pointer. Used for current location, turn-by-turn navigation, heading and start route buttons in map apps.

pointer-hand.context: A hand with the index finger pointing up. The link or clickable cursor in browsers, and a tap or click here hint in tutorials and onboarding.

redirect.context: An arrow that runs right along the bottom, then turns off diagonally up to the right. Used for URL redirects, rerouting traffic, forwarding calls and detours.

redo.context: A hooked arrow curving forward to the right. The redo action in editors and toolbars, used to repeat or restore the last undone change.

refresh-ccw.context: A circular arrow turning counter-clockwise. Used for reload, sync, reset, try again and restore to an earlier state.

repeat.context: Two arrows following each other around a rectangular loop. The repeat or loop control in music and video players, and a mark for recurring events and repeated tasks.

repeat-once.context: A repeat loop with a small figure 1 in the middle. The repeat one track control in music and podcast players.

reply.context: An arrow with a curved tail pointing back to the left. The reply action in email, comments, chat and forum threads.

reply-all.context: Two stacked curved arrows pointing back to the left. The reply to all action in email clients and group conversations.

rotate-ccw.context: A three-quarter circular arrow turning counter-clockwise. Used to rotate an image or page left by 90 degrees, and for turn left or rewind rotation.

rotate-cw.context: A three-quarter circular arrow turning clockwise. Used to rotate an image or page right by 90 degrees, refresh-style actions and spin controls.

route.context: Two small circles joined by a path that steps back and forth between them. Used for routes, trips, delivery tracking, directions and journey planning in map and logistics apps.

shuffle.context: Two smoothly curved arrows that cross in the middle and both point right. The shuffle control in music and video players, and a mark for random order.

sort-ascending.context: An up arrow beside a stack of bars that grow from short to long. Used for sort ascending in tables and lists: A to Z, lowest to highest, oldest first.

sort-descending.context: A down arrow beside a stack of bars that shrink from long to short. Used for sort descending in tables and lists: Z to A, highest to lowest, newest first.

split.context: A single line that rises and splits into two arrows pointing to the upper left and upper right. Used for split, diverge, divide traffic or data, and A/B paths.

step-into.context: An arrow pointing down toward a small circle below it. The step into command in code debuggers, and a mark for going one level deeper.

step-out.context: An arrow rising up away from a small circle below it. The step out command in code debuggers, and a mark for going back up one level.

swap-horizontal.context: Two horizontal arrows on separate lines pointing in opposite directions. Used for swap, exchange, transfer, currency conversion and switching two values.

swap-vertical.context: Two vertical arrows side by side pointing in opposite directions. Used for swap, reorder, sort toggles, data transfer and send and receive.

target.context: A bullseye of two rings around a centre dot. Used for goals, objectives, targets and KPIs, aim and focus, and audience targeting in marketing tools.

trending-down.context: A zigzag line that falls from the upper left to an arrow at the lower right. Used for falling prices, declining sales, losses and negative change in charts and dashboards.

trending-up.context: A zigzag line that rises from the lower left to an arrow at the upper right. Used for growth, rising sales, profit, trending content and positive change in charts and dashboards.

u-turn-left.context: An arrow that goes up, curves over and comes back down on the left. Used for U-turn directions in maps and driving apps, turning around and going back.

u-turn-right.context: An arrow that goes up, curves over and comes back down on the right. Used for U-turn directions in maps and driving apps, and for turning around on the right-hand side.

undo.context: A hooked arrow curving back to the left. The undo action in editors and toolbars, used to reverse the last change or step back in history.

zoom-in.context: A magnifying glass with a plus sign in the lens. Used to zoom in on maps, images, documents and canvases, and for enlarge or magnify controls.

zoom-out.context: A magnifying glass with a minus sign in the lens. Used to zoom out on maps, images, documents and canvases, and for reduce or see more controls.
